facts: The research article titled "Large Language Models Meet NLP: A Survey" was published in 2025.
The article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science.
The authors of the article include Libo Qin and Philip S. Yu.
The article spans pages 1 to 35.
This study investigates the application of large language models (LLMs) in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks.
The research introduces a unified taxonomy categorizing LLMs into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The study highlights new frontiers and challenges in the field of NLP.
The research aims to inspire further advancements in the development of effective LLMs.
This paper surveys Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications in Natural Language Processing (NLP).
The study categorizes LLM applications into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
It introduces a new taxonomy for understanding LLMs in NLP.
The authors aim to inspire further advancements in LLM-based NLP.
The parameter-frozen paradigm includes zero-shot learning and few-shot learning.
Zero-shot learning is the most resource-efficient with strong out-of-domain generalization.
Full-parameter tuning offers the best in-domain performance but is the least efficient.
Parameter-efficient tuning can sometimes surpass full-parameter tuning under limited resources.
The text outlines various Natural Language Processing (NLP) understanding tasks, including Semantic Analysis, Information Extraction, Dialogue Understanding, and Table Understanding.
Sentiment analysis is identified as a key NLP function that employs zero-shot and few-shot learning techniques.
Information Extraction focuses on extracting structured data from text and uses similar learning paradigms to improve accuracy.
Dialogue Understanding utilizes zero-shot and few-shot learning to enhance interaction capabilities in spoken language understanding.
LLMs like GPT-3 excel in zero-shot learning for Summarization.
Models like CodeT5+ and CodeGemma lead advancements in Code Generation.
LLMs improve translation accuracy through zero-shot and few-shot learning in Machine Translation.
Parameter-tuning techniques enhance the reasoning abilities of LLMs in Mathematical Reasoning.
Multilingual LLMs are being enhanced to support over 7,000 languages.
Challenges include improving performance in low-resource languages.
X-of-thought (XoT) techniques are needed for advanced logical reasoning.
Long Chain-of-Thought (Long-CoT) methods are being developed for deeper reasoning.
The work introduces a unified taxonomy that differentiates between parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The authors received grants from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
The research includes notable models such as "Diaggpt," "Cabinet," TableGPT, and Codet5.
The work aims to maintain a publicly accessible resource website for ongoing developments in LLMs.
